items.q: How do I book a charter?
items.a: Book online through our booking page, or call or text Capt. Chad at (386) 853-4814. Tell him what you're after (inshore, redfish, nearshore, shark fishing or a dolphin tour) and he'll match the trip to the tide.

items.q: How much does a charter cost?
items.a: Inshore trips start at $475 for 4 hours, nearshore at $550, shark trips at $575 and the dolphin and manatee tour is $375 for the whole group. Each price covers a set number of guests, with a small charge for each extra guest up to 6. See all trip prices.

items.q: How long are the trips and when do they start?
items.a: Inshore trips run 4 hours (7:00 AM or 11:30 AM) or 6 hours (6:00 AM). Nearshore trips leave at 7:00 AM for 4 or 6 hours. Shark trips run 3 hours (8:00 AM or noon) or 6 hours. The dolphin tour is 2 hours at 9:00 AM.

items.q: Do you require a deposit to book?
items.a: Most trips require a deposit to hold your date. Book online or call Capt. Chad to confirm the deposit for your trip.

items.q: What's your cancellation policy?
items.a: If you need to cancel or reschedule, give Capt. Chad as much notice as possible so he can rebook the slot. Weather cancellations are fully refunded or rescheduled.

items.q: Do you offer gift cards?
items.a: Yes. Gift cards are available on our booking page, or call Capt. Chad at (386) 853-4814.

items.q: What's included in the trip price?
items.a: Your Florida fishing license, all rods, reels, tackle and bait, and fish cleaning for in season species. Every trip is private, so the price is for your group, not per person.

items.q: Do I need a fishing license?
items.a: No. Every charter includes your Florida fishing license, so there's nothing to buy beforehand.

items.q: What should I bring?
items.a: Your own food and drinks (no glass), sunscreen (no spray), polarized sunglasses and sun protective clothing like a hat or hooded shirt. Bug spray helps on evening trips.

items.q: Can we bring beer?
items.a: Yes, in moderation. Just no glass bottles on the boat.

items.q: Is there a bathroom on the boat?
items.a: No. The 22' Sundance skiff doesn't have a bathroom on board, so plan accordingly before you step aboard.

items.q: Can I bring my own rod?
items.a: Yes. Bring a favorite rod and reel and Capt. Chad will work with your setup. Every charter already includes rods, tackle and bait.

items.q: Are your trips good for kids?
items.a: Yes. Kids fish with us all the time, and guests regularly mention how patient Capt. Chad is with them, from baiting hooks to untangling lines. Inshore trips run in calm, protected water, which makes them the easiest first trip.

items.q: How many people can you take?
items.a: Up to 6 guests per trip. Every trip is private, just your group and the captain, never combined with another party.

items.q: What happens if the weather is bad?
items.a: If conditions aren't safe to run, Capt. Chad will reschedule your trip or refund you. He'd rather move a date than put anyone on the water in bad weather.

items.q: Do you run offshore or deep sea trips?
items.a: No. Capt. Chad runs inshore trips in the lagoons and nearshore trips up to about 6 miles off the beach, out of Ponce Inlet.

items.q: Do people get seasick?
items.a: Rarely. Inshore trips stay in calm, protected water, and nearshore trips stay within about 6 miles of the beach. If you're prone to motion sickness, book an inshore trip.

items.q: Are life jackets provided?
items.a: Yes. Every charter carries the required U.S. Coast Guard safety gear, including life jackets for adults and children. Let Capt. Chad know if kids will be on board.

items.q: Can we book a trip without fishing?
items.a: Yes. Our dolphin and manatee tour is a 2 hour cruise on the Indian River Lagoon, and bioluminescence tours run on warm nights when the glow is on.

items.q: What's biting right now?
items.a: It changes with the tide and the season. Redfish are around every month, snook lead the summer, and sheepshead take over the bridges in winter. Our monthly fishing reports show what we've actually been catching.

items.q: What's the best time of year to fish New Smyrna Beach and Daytona?
items.a: Fishing runs year round. Spring brings redfish and cobia, summer turns on snook and tarpon, fall is prime for oversized redfish, flounder and drum, and winter brings sheepshead to the docks and bridges.

items.q: Do you keep fish?
items.a: Yes, for in season species like redfish, trout, flounder and sheepshead, following Florida's size and bag limits. Legal sharks can be kept too, within the same rules.

items.q: What do you catch nearshore?
items.a: Kingfish, flounder, sand trout and jacks, plus tarpon and cobia when they're running. Blacktip sharks are often around the beach in the warm months. See nearshore fishing.

items.q: When can I book a shark trip?
items.a: Shark trips run May 1 through November 1, and summer is peak. See shark fishing.

items.q: Where do the trips leave from?
items.a: New Smyrna Beach, FL, a short drive south of Daytona Beach, with quick access to the Indian River Lagoon, Mosquito Lagoon, Ponce Inlet and the nearshore Atlantic.

items.q: How early should we arrive?
items.a: Plan to arrive 10 to 15 minutes before your departure time so Capt. Chad can run through the safety basics and get everyone settled.
